To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BDNF induces the ERK5- MEF2-NT3 signaling pathway in a temporally specific pattern in the developing cerebellum, and that the ERK5 - MEF2- NT3 pathway mediates the survival effect of BDNF on newly generated, but nor mature, granule cells.
BDNF promotes survival of newly generated neurons in the developing mammal brain by activating the ERK5-myocyte enhancer factor-NT-3 pathway.
the BDNF-induced ERK5-ME2-NT- 3 signaling pathway is required for the survival of newly formed granule cells in the cerebellum.

the mechanisms of neuronal survival and death during development and in adult neurodegenerative diseases.
the mechanisms underlying the development, maintenance and plasticity of neural circuits.
the mechanisms that underlie the development of the mammalian nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal specificity of BDNF-induced neuron survival is mediated through a novel ERK5-MEKF2-NT- 3 signaling mechanism.
BDNF-induced NT-3 expression is a novel mechanism underlying the temporally specific antiapoptotic function of neurotrophines in the developing cerebellum.
ERK5-ME2-NT3 signaling pathway is a key mechanism for the temporal specificity of BDNF-induced neuronal survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal specificity by BDNF in promoting survival of granule neurons is mediated by a signaling pathway involving ERK5 and MEF2, which induces transcription of NT-3, a novel gene target.
BDNF induces the ERK5-myocyte enhancer factor-2 (MEF2)-neurotrophin- 3 signaling pathway in newly born granule neurons, which is required for the antiapoptosis effect of BDNF in these neurons.

we have characterized a novel mechanism that mediates the temporal specificity of neurotrophic action by which BDNFs selectively promotes the survival and differentiation of newly generated neurons in the developing brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ERK5/MAPK signaling pathway is involved in the regulation of neurogenesis in the developing brain.
the ERK5 signaling pathway mediates the survival-promoting effects of BDNF in the newly generated granule neuron population in the developing cerebellum.

neurotrophins induce the survival of newly formed, but not mature neurons in the cerebellum, through a mechanism that is dependent on the activation of the ERK5 pathway, which leads to the activation of MEF2, and the subsequent induction of NT-3 expression in the neurons.
